region: Meghalaya, Brahmaputra valley and upper Assam
title: India — The Khasi Forests and the Brahmaputra's Islands
subtitle: Sacred groves, Jaintia monoliths, a foothill jungle camp, Ahom burial mounds and Majuli's monasteries
summary: A 15-day loop through the Khasi and Jaintia hills and the Brahmaputra valley with village homestays, a walk-in jungle camp, Kaziranga and a stay on Majuli, designed to avoid Manipur and border strips.
introduction: Fifteen days along the Brahmaputra valley and the Khasi and Jaintia hills, built around places that state-level tours skip: a sacred forest guarded by Khasi custom, the Laitlum canyon rim, the Pnar monolith fields of Nartiang, a guided jungle walk and tented camp on the Jia Bhoreli, Ahom royal burial mounds inscribed by UNESCO in 2024, and a stay on Majuli, the river island where Vaishnavite monasteries (satras) and Mising stilt villages share the floodplain. A hired driver links the stops; walks, rafting and safaris are guided. The route deliberately avoids Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram, the Bangladesh border strip and Arunachal's China border, which official advisories flag.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman was self-drive desert and mountain camping in an empty country. This is a green, populous and river-dominated region where a hired driver is the legal and sensible norm, and the interest lies in staying with Khasi, Pnar and Mising host families and in two forest/river environments rather than open desert.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard north-east packages run Shillong, Cherrapunji, Kaziranga and Majuli day trips. This plan skips the border-adjacent waterfalls and root-bridge circuit, uses village homestays, a walk-in foothill camp, Charaideo's burial mounds and a possible overlap with the Mising spring festival.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination offers a river island with working monasteries, a UNESCO royal burial landscape inscribed in 2024 and community-protected sacred forest in one route, all with no permit beyond the e-Visa.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound and Day 15 arrival; Days 2 and 14 add Delhi domestic connections.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Dry season for Kaziranga and Nameri, clear days on the Khasi plateau, and Day 12 lands on Wednesday 17 February, the likely Mising Ali-Ai-Ligang date (inferred from the first-Wednesday-of-Phagun rule seen in 2026, not confirmed). Ramadan starts about 8 February.

februarySuitability.summary: Dry, cool and clear in the hills, with morning fog in the valley; lowest rain of the year and the best weather for forest walks and rafting.

marchSuitability.summary: Warmer and more humid, with pre-monsoon thunderstorms from late March; rhino grass is shorter after burning but heat and haze rise. The festival overlap is lost.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow on the route. Himalayan passes such as Sela in Arunachal are outside the route.
climate.airQuality: Generally fair; Guwahati traffic dust and crop-burning haze can reduce visibility.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Kaziranga's dry-season window; rhino and elephant are easiest to see in short grass after annual burning, from about February onward.

climate.ramadan2027: Starts about 8 Feb; limited impact because the route is mostly Hindu, Khasi, Pnar and Mising areas; some Muslim-run restaurants in Guwahati and Hajo may adjust hours.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: the Losar Tibetan new year is celebrated by Buddhist communities in Arunachal and Sikkim, outside this route.
climate.tourismDemand: Kaziranga is busy Jan-Mar (22,000 visitors in 26 days after the Oct 2026 reopening per press); homestays book out near weekends.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Paris-Delhi fares in February are typically moderate; Valentine's and wedding-season weekends can raise domestic fares.

geography.summary: A plateau of Khasi and Jaintia hills rising from the Brahmaputra floodplain, then riverine grassland, foothill jungle and a river island.
geography.distinctive: Community-protected sacred forests on the Khasi plateau, a foothill rainforest accessible only on foot at Nameri, and Majuli, a continuously reshaped river island.

travelStyle.summary: A hired driver with guided walks and safaris; the foothill camp is the only camping.

transport.summary: One hired car with driver from Guwahati to Dibrugarh, an Assam ferry to Majuli and two domestic flights.

modes.description: Innova-class vehicle for four plus bags; driver handles hill roads, fuel and tolls.
Neamati-Majuli vehicle ferry, about 1 h; last crossings mid/late afternoon.
Delhi-Guwahati and Dibrugarh-Delhi on IndiGo or Air India.

transport.carRental: Self-drive hire is unusual in the region; hire a car with driver through a registered Guwahati operator. Meghalaya and Assam taxi unions restrict outside vehicles for local sightseeing.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is possible on paper but not recommended: unfamiliar traffic, livestock, fog, landslides and the common after-accident hostility described by FCDO.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: FCDO states a UK licence plus a 1949-convention IDP is required; for other nationalities check whether the home licence plus IDP is valid in India.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two travellers hold car licences, two none: the hired driver removes any licence issue.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: Nobody may ride a motorcycle or scooter without the correct licence; legal alternatives are hired driver, guided jeep or pillion with a licensed guide.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Hired car with driver for the whole loop; two licence holders could share only if a rental contract allowed it, which is not planned.

accommodation.summary: Village homestays in Meghalaya and Majuli, a tented eco-camp at Nameri, lodges at Kaziranga and tea-estate bungalows.

camping.summary: Only organised tented camps (Nameri); no wild camping.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Walks of 2-3 h with steps at Laitlum and Nameri; several 4-5.5 h driving days.

itinerary.summary: Guwahati, Khasi and Jaintia hills, north-bank Assam, Nameri, Kaziranga, Majuli and upper Assam; flexible Days 10 and 14.

days.title: Departure to Delhi
activities: Fly Paris to Delhi (direct or via a Gulf hub).
Complete the e-arrival card and the Air Suvidha health form within the required window before landing.
days.practical: Apply for the e-Visa at least 2-3 weeks ahead (window opens 120 days before arrival). Carry insurance papers.

days.title: Delhi to the Brahmaputra
activities: Land in Delhi, connect to Guwahati (GAU), ~2 h 40 min.
Taxi to the centre; ferry to Umananda island at dusk, Fancy Bazar street food and an Assamese thali.
days.practical: Allow 3-4 h minimum for the Delhi connection (Terminal change/immigration).

days.title: Into the Khasi hills
activities: Drive up the Shillong road (NH6) into the Khasi Hills.
Afternoon guided walk in Mawphlang sacred forest; the local guide explains the taboo on removing anything.
Dinner with the host family.
days.practical: Cool evenings; pack a fleece. Use a Meghalaya-registered taxi for local sightseeing if the driver advises.

days.title: Laitlum canyon trail
activities: Drive to Laitlum and walk the stepped trail along the canyon rim and down to the first village.
Return via Smit villages and a Khasi market if open.
days.practical: Check locally for any inter-state boundary or bandh disruption before leaving.

days.title: Pnar monolith country
activities: Cross the plateau to the Jaintia Hills.
Walk the Nartiang monolith fields and old temple; evening in a Jowai-area homestay.
days.practical: Roads are slow; avoid driving after dark.

days.title: Back to the Brahmaputra
activities: Descend to Guwahati and cross the river.
Afternoon at Hajo's shrines and Sualkuchi's silk looms.
days.culturalHighlight: Hajo shared pilgrimage site; Sualkuchi weaving
days.practical: Longest early drive; traffic around Guwahati is heavy.

days.title: North to the foothills
activities: Drive along the north bank to the Jia Bhoreli.
Arrive at the Nameri eco-camp for a first walk with a guide.
days.geographicalHighlight: Foothill forest on the Arunachal boundary
days.practical: Longest driving day of the trip; leave at dawn.

days.title: Jia Bhoreli day
activities: Early guided walk for birds (confirm any forest-guard requirement with the camp).
Afternoon rafting on the river.
days.practical: Dry-season flows are gentler; the trip is mostly drifting rather than whitewater.

days.title: Across to Kaziranga
activities: Drive south through Tezpur and over the river.
Afternoon jeep safari in the Central (Kohora) range.

days.title: Rhinos at dawn
activities: Dawn safari in the Western range, then slow day: village walk, rest, tea.
Optional second afternoon safari.

days.title: River island arrival
activities: Drive to Jorhat and Neamati ghat; ferry crossing to Majuli.
Evening in a Mising stilt-house homestay.
days.practical: Last ferry is mid/late afternoon; leave Kaziranga by 09:30.

days.title: Satras and Mising villages
activities: Visit two or three satras and a mask-making workshop.
If it falls this week, join local Ali-Ai-Ligang celebrations (first Wednesday of Phagun, inferred about 17 Feb 2027; not confirmed).
days.practical: Festival date is derived from the 2026 rule and must be rechecked.

days.title: Ahom royal burial mounds
activities: Ferry to Neamati, drive to Sivasagar and Charaideo Moidams.
Continue to a tea-estate bungalow near Dibrugarh.
days.practical: Check for local bandh or political-event closures on the day.

days.title: Tea country and departure
activities: Morning tea-estate walk and a factory visit.
Afternoon flight to Delhi, connection to Paris overnight.
days.practical: Flexible day: shorten if the evening flight shifts.

activities: Land in Paris.

security.summary: The route is a Meghalaya-Assam loop that stays out of Manipur (red/against all but essential), Nagaland and Mizoram (Dutch orange), the Bangladesh border strip (Dutch orange), the Myanmar border and Arunachal's China border. No advisory reviewed advises against travel to the route regions. Residual risks are insurgent-linked incidents, bandhs and inter-state boundary flare-ups, and road safety.
security.assessedRoute: Guwahati, Mawphlang, Laitlum, Nartiang (Meghalaya, all roughly 25 km or more north of the Bangladesh border by estimate), Hajo, Nameri, Kaziranga, Majuli, Charaideo/Sivasagar and Dibrugarh (Assam). Excludes Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram, Tripura, Arunachal border districts, Dawki/Shnongpdeng/Mawlynnong/Cherrapunji-Nongriat area and Mukroh/Assam-Meghalaya boundary villages.

advisories.routeImpact: Route avoids Manipur and border strips; keep to main roads and check locally

advisories.routeImpact: Route avoids Nagaland and Mizoram and stays away from the Bangladesh and China border areas; strip width is undefined, so the buffer is a precaution

conflictRisk.note: No active conflict on the route, but inter-state boundary skirmishes (Assam-Meghalaya), bandhs and ethnic tension in the Northeast can start at short notice.

terrorismRisk.note: Low-level insurgent activity in upper Assam (Dibrugarh/Sivasagar area) has occurred around national days; the window avoids 26 January and 15 August but advisories should be rechecked.

kidnappingRisk.note: No advisory reviewed highlights tourist kidnapping on the assessed route; keep to registered operators and hotels.

regionalRestrictions: Nagaland needs a Protected Area Permit via e-FRRO outside 26 Nov-15 Dec (reported Feb and Nov 2026); Netherlands orange: not in this route.
Arunachal Pradesh needs a PAP via an approved operator (USD 30); not in this route.
Meghalaya is introducing ILP-style tourist registration; treatment of foreigners unclear in 2026 reports; confirm with hosts and the Meghalaya tourism office.
Satellite phones and GPS devices need prior authorisation (France: banned without it).
Foreigners must register with the Foreigners Registration Officer in some states; hotels file Form C.
ordinaryRisks: High road-death rate; avoid night driving and fog
Livestock and crowds on roads; dispute after accidents can turn hostile
Food and water hygiene; Ebola self-declaration still required on arrival in 2026
Earthquake zone; landslides on hill roads
Fog delays flights and drives in Feb
security.medicalAccess: Good private hospitals in Guwahati (GMCH, private hospitals), adequate in Shillong, Jorhat and Dibrugarh (Assam Medical College), basic clinics elsewhere. Nameri, Mawphlang and Majuli are 1-3 h from hospitals. Evacuation by road/ air from Guwahati or Dibrugarh.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Travel against advice voids FCDO-aligned policies. Choose a policy with medical evacuation and trekking cover; no altitude above ~2,000 m on this route.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check FCDO, Netherlands, France, Smartraveller and US advisories before booking and two weeks before departure; specific triggers: any Dutch/FCDO advisory covering Assam or Meghalaya, bandh calls, Assam-Meghalaya boundary incidents, changes to Meghalaya's foreigner registration, changes to the PAP regime.

practicalRequirements.visa: India e-Tourist visa for eligible nationalities (175 listed); 30-day fee US$25 July-March plus bank charge; apply at least 4 days and up to 120 days before arrival; conditional on nationality.
practicalRequirements.entry: Arrival via Delhi on the e-Visa (Guwahati also designated); e-arrival card and the 2026 Ebola self-declaration form on the Air Suvidha portal. Dibrugarh was not in the e-Visa airport list for entry, only used for departure.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: At least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages (FCDO and e-Visa rules).
permits: No Protected Area Permit is needed for this route.
Nagaland PAP mandatory outside 26 Nov-15 Dec (not used).
Arunachal PAP USD 30 via approved operator (not used).
Meghalaya ILP-style registration for visitors is being introduced; confirm for foreigners.
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with medical evacuation and trekking cover; avoid policies excluding the north-east.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile data works in towns; weak or absent in Nameri, Mawphlang and Majuli villages; GPS devices and satellite phones need permission.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cash needed in homestays and villages; ATMs in Guwahati, Jorhat and Dibrugarh.
practicalRequirements.medical: Routine vaccines, hepatitis A, typhoid; malaria risk low in dry season (confirm with a travel clinic); carry rehydration salts.
